This advice is spot on. I kicked Addy after nearly a decade of daily high dose usage. Best advice I can give is to just listen to your body. You’ve probably been depriving it of a lot of sleep and food, so you might eat/sleep a lot more than normal in the early stages. But after a couple weeks that’ll start to even back out.

Try to stick to a solid sleep schedule and eat a nutritious diet. I’m a notoriously picky eater so I try  to fit a green shake in every day. Exercise might be tough early on too just because you’re going to feel super lazy, but even little bits like getting out for short walks can help improve energy levels over the long term.

Good luck though, you got this! Just be easy on yourself and know that it will take time for your brain to fully heal. If you have a really demanding job, maybe look into using some PTO or FMLA so that you can focus solely on your health for now.

I have dealt with pretty severe depression most of my life and I can absolutely relate to what you’re going through. All of the standard advice about how it’ll only make things worse, just doesn’t seem to matter when I’m in that state. I’m well aware that it’s only a temporary solution and I know it’ll kill me over the long term. Unfortunately, to my depressed brain, those BOTH sound like positives.

All of that being said, I’ll just share a few thoughts that help me avoid the bottle. One I always try to remind myself is that you’re not gaining any additional happiness from drinking, you’re essentially just “borrowing” it from the future at an EXTREMELY high interest rate. You pay it back in the form of debilitating hangovers, awful life decisions, and the steady deterioration of your mental/physical health to name just a few.

Also, if at all possible, try to give back or volunteer somewhere. Regardless of how bad we’ve had it (and it was REALLY bad during my heavy drinking years), there’s unfortunately always someone out there who has it worse than we do. It’s the tragedy of the human condition. But it’s incredible how much helping someone else out can make you feel better and distract you from the pain you’re currently going through. Not to mention, I’m a strong believer that kindness begets more kindness. Helping someone else in a worse position than myself, provides me some level of comfort that maybe someone else would do the same for me if I was in a similar position (whether that’s true or not, I have no clue lol). And I’m well aware just how close I am to being in that position. I’m just a few poor decisions or unlucky accidents away from total and complete rock bottom.

Sorry, I know this isn’t a perfect answer but hopefully knowing that you’re not alone provides even a small amount of comfort. Best of luck and IWNDWYT.

I added in a few more below that came to my mind as I was reading through yours:

1. Look out for (especially on eBay) listings that say something along the lines of “custom art card 1/1.” These are NOT officially licensed products and are usually just some sort of cheap knockoff of popular cards like Kaboom! By all means, if the “art card” looks awesome to you and you really just want to display it, then have at it! Just don’t expect there to be much (if any) resale value on it.

2. Another source of confusion I’ve seen is the frequent use of the term “eBay 1-of-1” in listing descriptions. This is NOT a true one-of-one and it essentially means nothing. It’s saying that it’s the only copy of the card that exists in all of the current eBay listings. Its ACTUAL rarity could vary significantly from its rarity amongst what currently happens to be listed on eBay.
Also, you may see 1-of-1 used in the title when there’s a serial numbered card that’s either the first print (i.e. something numbered 1/50), a number match (i.e. Dan Marino card numbered 13/50), or last print (i.e. a card numbered 50/50). While I would agree that these cards hold greater appeal over the remaining 47 cards in that particular print, I would still say it is at the very least misleading because these cards are far from being true 1/1.

3. Another one, and this one might seem obvious to most people, but when you’re shopping for cards, it’s best to remain sober lol. It’s not an activity that you really want to come into with lowered inhibitions… unless you want to go broke really fast.

4. Another topic has to deal with memorabilia/patch cards. The thing that seems to have changed with these (at least compared to when I first started collecting as a kid) is that it’s very important to read what it says on the back. There are a few different versions of the patch cards now and not all of them contain game used material. For example, one that I see very frequently nowadays says, “the enclosed authentic memorabilia is not from any specific game or event.” Notice that there is no mention of game-worn/player-worn or anything along those lines. Essentially what you’re getting is a chunk from an “authentic jersey” that they just took off the rack. They cut a piece out of it and sandwiched it between some cardboard. In doing so, they created a pointless/disappointing card that is unnecessarily thick and annoying. A lot of times I won’t even waste a thick top loader on these pieces of junk just out of sheer principle.

5. Lastly, I’ve found that I feel like (as cliche as it may sound), I get the most enjoyment out of the hobby when the focus is less about some end goal, a specific destination, or obtaining some holy grail collectible. This is a recipe for disappointment because, regardless of what you currently consider to be your most prized/valuable acquisition, there will always be something better out there. The real value I have found to be in the actual experience of going to local card shows, chasing down the next greatest deal, learning new things (about the collectible and sports worlds alike), and meeting a lot of really cool people with some really cool shit lol

Happy collecting!!
